steps.title: Open UniFi Access
steps.body: Open the console in your browser (or via unifi.ui.com) and start the Access application.

steps.title: Create an API token
steps.body: Go to Settings › General › Advanced › API Token and click Create New. Name it e.g. “License Plate Importer”.

steps.title: Give it user rights
steps.body: Select at least View and Edit for Users (and User Groups), and choose a validity that suits you.

steps.title: Copy the token
steps.body: The token is shown only once. Paste it into the field on the left.

steps.title: Enter the address
steps.body: Use the console's local IP address. This server must reach it on port 12445 (HTTPS).

steps.title: Test
steps.body: Click Test. When the connection works, save the console and click Read to load its existing plates.

backup.title: Backup & restore
backup.description: Encrypted full and incremental backups to your own servers, and restore from them.
backup.needPassphrase: Set a backup passphrase and add a backup location before the first backup.
backup.targetsHint: Every backup is sent to each active location.
backup.noTargets: No backup location yet. Add a server reached with SCP (SSH), FTPS or FTP.
backup.confirmDelete: Delete the location {{name}}? The backups on that server stay where they are.
how: A full backup contains all vehicles, consoles, users, settings, API keys and the audit log.
An incremental backup only contains what changed since the previous backup on that location, so it is small and fast.
Every backup is encrypted with AES-256 using your passphrase before it leaves this server.
Restoring an incremental backup automatically uses the full backup and the incremental backups before it.
On a new server: install with install.sh --restore, or add the location here and restore from the list.
backup.uploadHint: Upload a backup file from your computer: a full backup, or a full backup together with its incremental backups.
backup.restoreWarning: All current data of this application (vehicles, consoles, users, settings, API keys, audit log) is replaced by the backup. A copy of the current data is saved on this server first. Nothing changes on the UniFi consoles.
backup.restorePassphraseHint: Leave empty when the backup was made with the current passphrase.
backup.restoreUnderstood: I understand that the current data will be replaced.
backup.noBackups: No backups found in this folder.
backup.chainHint: An incremental backup can only be restored while its full backup and the incremental backups in between are present (marked incomplete otherwise).
backup.encryptionHint: The passphrase encrypts every backup. Without it a backup cannot be restored, also not by us.
backup.passphraseHint: At least 12 characters. Store it in your password manager: you need it to restore on a new server.
backup.passphraseChangeHint: Leave empty to keep the current passphrase. After a change, the next backup is a full backup; older backups keep their old passphrase.
backup.storeSafely: Store this passphrase in your password manager before saving.
backup.scheduleHint: Times are in the time zone of this server. A missed backup (server off) is made within 6 hours, otherwise at the next moment.

schedule.fullHint: Starts a new chain. Weekly is a good default.
schedule.incrementalHint: Only the changes since the previous backup. Daily or hourly.

backup.keepFull: Full backups to keep per location
backup.keepFullHint: Older full backups are deleted from the server together with their incremental backups.
backup.sshKeyHelp: For SCP locations with key sign-in: add this public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the backup user on the server.
backup.newSshKeyConfirm: Create a new SSH key? Locations that use the current key stop working until the new public key is added on the server.
backup.ftpWarning: Plain FTP sends the password unencrypted. The backup file itself is always encrypted, but prefer SCP or FTPS.
backup.remotePathHint: Created when it does not exist. Relative to the home folder unless it starts with /.
backup.verifyTlsHint: Switch off only for a self-signed certificate on your own network.
backup.passiveHint: Needed behind most firewalls and NAT.
backup.enabledHint: Inactive locations receive no backups but can still be used to restore.
backup.testOk_one: Connected and able to write. {{count}} backup found.
backup.testOk_other: Connected and able to write. {{count}} backups found.
backup.hostKeyHelp: Trusted on the first connection. A different key later is refused, so nobody can pose as your server.

scp.title: SCP (SSH)
scp.body: Recommended. Works with any Linux server or NAS with SSH (Synology, QNAP, TrueNAS). Uses SFTP when the server offers it, otherwise classic scp.

ftps.title: FTPS
ftps.body: FTP over TLS 1.2 or newer. Explicit TLS is the common choice; use implicit for servers that only listen on port 990.

ftp.title: FTP
ftp.body: For old servers only. The backup file is encrypted, but the sign-in is not.

security.title: Security
security.description: Sessions, sign-in protection and the signed-in users.

security.sessionHoursHint: After this, signing in again is required.
security.rateHint: Slows down password guessing and runaway integrations.

security.httpsOk: The application is reached over HTTPS.

security.secretKeyOk: A strong secret key encrypts the stored passwords and tokens.

security.encryptedNote: Console tokens, SMTP, SSO and backup passwords and the backup passphrase are stored encrypted (AES). API keys and user passwords are only stored as a hash.
